name: Design C: Python-first 2.5D on the flat map, no globe library; pydeck/MapLibre globe as a gated later phase
status: Research design; nothing ships. Only this file was written; other agents' uncommitted prototype edits were left alone.

host.task_constraints_describe: payload/, desktop/, self-test, 50 MiB whole-repo zipball and rule 2 installers describe the parked app.
host.current_host: Since D27 (2026-10-14) the product is a static website built by Python every 10 min (website.yml:15) and served by GitHub Pages. This design targets the app as the task states; website_mapping says what carries over.
website_mapping: No self-test, zipball or installer applies; a merge to main is live in about 10 min (AGENTS.md).
Vendored bytes and phone performance decide the library, not the zipball cap (supervisor log, ARCHITECTURE SHIFT).
Producers: website/gridded.py and build.py. Hand-written browser code: map.js and base.html:167-168 (rule 4).
Pages: 1 GB per site, 100 GB/month soft (gh-pages-1, -2). Actions terms (gh-terms-1, -3) and the schedule floor (gh-sched-1, -4) are open owner or legal items.

summary: Recommended first build, C2: no globe library. Python builds fixed-region PNG layers and fixed-transect SVG profiles: MRMS echo-top height classes from 11 of the 33 MSL levels (below-ground levels masked with a Python-built terrain grid), GOES ACHA cloud-top height classes (satellite estimate, not corrected for parallax) and a GOES Band 13 picture. The browser shows them as Leaflet image overlays on the vendored Leaflet 1.9.4 map and runs 6 new small duties. C1 (pydeck to a MapLibre globe with deck.gl) is a gated Phase 5 decision: pydeck 0.9.3 has no GlobeView class, deck.gl 9.4.0 has no VolumeLayer, deck.gl marks GlobeView experimental, pydeck's HTML loads third-party resources even offline, and the app would need numpy (a new installer).
recommendation: C2 first. C1 only if the owner approves D-G1 and duties G1-G8. Neither option renders true 3D storm volumes; the owner's 3D wish is met only in part by either.

C2_flat_map_2_5d.what_it_is: Leaflet 1.9.4 (already vendored) with Python-built image overlays and SVG profiles. No globe, no WebGL, no new library.
cannot_do_that_owner_asked: Rotate, tilt or orbit; show storm columns or volumes in 3D.
Place cloud tops at true height over terrain: they are drawn as height classes, with the uncorrected offset disclosed (parallax.json).
Look like a globe (it stays a Mercator map).
Profile any clicked line: a static site shows only fixed, pre-built transects.
Animate between frames: frames are 10-minute pictures; no temporal or level interpolation (rule 5).
C2_flat_map_2_5d.protects: Rule 4 and D1 (Python builds all data; no framework; no new library); the no-CDN rule; offline states (every file comes from the site); phone bytes (0.66 MB per build); honest estimate labels; reuse of website/gridded.py.

C1_globe_pydeck_maplibre.what_it_is: pydeck 0.9.3 as a Python spec builder driving a MapLibre globe projection with deck.gl 9.4.0 layers, in a custom page.
cannot_do_that_owner_asked: Show volumes without custom WebGL/GLSL: deck.gl 9.4.0 dist.min.js has 0 matches for VolumeLayer (live, 2026-10-17); setTexture3DData has 1, so the volume shader would be hand-written.

Offer a pydeck 'GlobeView': none exists in pydeck 0.9.3. deck.py lines 93-95: 'Map projection to use with map_provider=maplibre. Values can be globe or mercator.' deck.gl's GlobeView page: 'This class is experimental'. MapLibre: 'Globe View or Globe Projection was released as part of MapLibre GL JS 5.0.0' (all live, 2026-10-17).

Run offline with pydeck's own page: index.j2 loads a Mapbox GL or Google Maps script (lines 6-10), Bootstrap and Font Awesome from maxcdn (11-12), MapLibre CSS from unpkg (13); the widget stylesheet is always jsDelivr (html.py:37, index.j2:15). offline=True inlines the 4,269,385 B bundle (html.py:49-53) but keeps those links.
Use pydeck's default basemap: map_styles.py points at basemaps.cartocdn.com, which D9 says needs a key.
Guarantee WebGL2 on crew laptops: WebView2 WebGL2 is not stated in the pages read; MSHTML has no WebGL2 (webgl-runtime.json).
C1_globe_pydeck_maplibre.protects: A real globe and 3D columns on desktops and tablets, and volumes, once parallax is corrected (plan Phase 2).

js_duties: E1 [existing; map.js:1400] Frame playback timer. Reason: frame advance is a timer in the viewer's browser.
E2 [existing; map.js:1449-1452] Scrub by pointer. Reason: pointer position exists only in the browser.
E3 [existing; map.js:1493] Layer menu open, close, tap-outside. Reason: DOM events.
E4 [existing] Town sheet and List show and hide on tap. Reason: DOM show and hide.
E5 [existing; map.js:1727-1730] Geolocation request and marker. Reason: navigator.geolocation exists only in the browser.
E6 [existing; map.js:116-119] Same-origin fetch of data/*.json with plain-words failure reasons. Reason: the browser makes the request.
E7 [existing; base.html:167-168, map.js:1682] Page-age check; warning past 25 min. Reason: the viewer's clock, not the build's.
N1 [C2 new] Layer switch and opacity for echo-top and cloud-top overlays. Reason: DOM control state; Python supplies legend and frame list.
N2 [C2 new] Rolling echo-top window on the existing timeline (reuses E1-E2). Reason: same timer; no new geometry.
N3 [C2 new] Show one pre-built transect SVG from three fixed. Reason: choosing a file is a DOM event.
N4 [C2 new] Per-layer 'could not load' text when an image or SVG fails. Reason: only the browser sees a failed request.
N5 [C2 new] Per-layer age clock, recalculated each minute. Reason: the viewer's clock; Python cannot know it.
N6 [C2 new] Accessible names and aria-pressed on new controls. Reason: attributes are set in the DOM.
G1 [C1 only] Load vendored globe modules; '3D view could not load' on failure. Reason: modules execute in the browser.
G2 [C1 only] WebGL2 probe before creating the globe. Reason: only the browser knows its GPU context.
G3 [C1 only] webglcontextlost and restored handling. Reason: GPU events exist only in the browser.
G4 [C1 only] Turn Python layer JSON into deck.gl layer props. Reason: hand-written glue between data and library.
G5 [C1 only] Fetch per-frame data and set layer data on time change. Reason: browser network and timing.
G6 [C1 only] Upload per-frame 3D textures for volumes. Reason: GPU upload is browser-only; no VolumeLayer means hand-written shader code.
G7 [C1 only] Vertical exaggeration control, labelled on screen. Reason: UI event setting a shader uniform.
G8 [C1 only] Reset-view button and keyboard camera keys. Reason: UI events; the library handles drag.
js_duty_counts: Existing 7 (E1-E7, approved in D28). C2 adds 6 (N1-N6), so C2 totals 13. C1 adds 8 (G1-G8), so the total with C1 is 21. Each duty is documented inline (rule 4).

integrity_policy: Exact versions only. Each vendored file's sha256 sits in a manifest that the build checks, and a test fails on mismatch. Files come from the site, never a CDN; a test finds no URL outside the site in built HTML, JS, CSS or JSON. SRI is unneeded for same-origin files. New versions need 14 days of age (proposal). No paid token or key in browser code (globe-libs.json). The app's Folium Leaflet 1.9.3 loads from jsDelivr with no integrity attribute (folium.py:27, read live); D23's 'Folium bundles Leaflet' is wrong and needs a correction entry.

offline_and_selftest.self_test: updater.selftest runs with NETWORK False and checks only HTTP status >= 400 (updater.py:141-142; default timeout 90 s, 122-158). /globe returns 200 whether or not the setting is on; only data routes and 3D controls depend on it. Live feeds read 'Off' (weather.py:517-518); 3D view reads 'Off (setting)'. No state is an all-clear. The self-test cannot see JavaScript or images; UI checks need a dev-only browser job (check-app.yml has no browser step).

evidence_kinds_and_freshness.loud_failure: Every product key must exist in sources.CONTRACTS and FRESH_SECONDS; a unit test fails on a missing key. The silent 3600 s default (weather.py:232) is not allowed.

alert_null_geometry: Matching unchanged: polygon contains the place; else UGC zone, county or fire-zone codes (rule 6; D10).
Alert with geometry: warning polygon outline with event name and end time. No fill colour by severity.

Null geometry matched by zone code: dashed NWS forecast-zone outline labelled 'Zone outline: the alert names this zone; the warning area is not given', plus marker and text at the town. Listed on the Now page with the D27 note.
Zone matched but no outline cached or fetch failed: marker and text 'Alert names this zone; outline not available'. Never omitted.
Town point check failed: 'Alerts not checked' with age (D27). Never 'no alerts'.
Parity test on three fixtures (zone-only, out-of-state code, cancel during an outage): map list and Now page list identical, 3 of 3; no town with a matching code reads 'no alert'.
No height or extrusion encoding of alerts, candidates or hazards; height encodings apply only to radar and satellite estimates.

storms_handling.levels: MRMS heights are heightAboveSea in metres, 500-19,000 m (mrms.json). Labels say 'above sea level'. Billings ground is 952 m (terrain.json): 0.5 km is 452 m below ground there; 1.0 km is 48 m above. mrms.json lists 'whether 0.5 km MSL lies below ground across Montana' as open, so P0 measures it.
storms_handling.below_ground_mask: A level is below ground when its height is under ground + 50 m (about twice the DEM-to-NWS gap at KBIL, 20-27 m, terrain.json). Below-ground levels never make an echo top and are not drawn. With no terrain grid the echo layer is Unavailable, not drawn unmasked.
storms_handling.no_data_codes: MRMS -99 and -999 both mean 'No radar data' (grey hatch). Meanings unverified (mrms.json; NSSL table returned HTTP 503). Never 0 dBZ; blank is never 'clear'. Tests: missing never becomes 0 dBZ; threshold_count_parity difference 0.
storms_handling.echo_top_definition: Highest valid level at or above 35 dBZ among the 11 levels, above the mask. Height is the level's own height, not interpolated. Height classes use one sequential palette, never a red-to-green severity ramp (rendering-options.json legend_rules). Valid columns with no level at or above 35 dBZ read 'No echo at 35 dBZ or more; not an all-clear'.
storms_handling.parallax: Does not apply to MRMS, a ground-grid product (mrms.json). It applies to satellite cloud tops only.
storms_handling.legend_echo: Radar echo top (estimate): the highest level at or above 35 dBZ, height above sea level, from NOAA MRMS data. Radar estimate only: not hail, not hail size, not damage. Grey = no radar data. Blank = no echo at 35 dBZ or more, which is not an all-clear. Heights are level heights, rounded up to the next MRMS level.
storms_handling.legend_cloud: Not corrected for cloud-top height. The cloud top is drawn where the satellite's ground grid puts it, away from the satellite (north-west or north-east of Montana): about 3 to 4 km off for a 2 km top, about 20 to 33 km off for a 12 to 15 km top. Estimated cloud-top height (satellite estimate). Cloud base is not observed. (parallax.json ui_legend_uncorrected_phase1, verbatim.)
storms_handling.no_interpolation: None across time (missing slot shows as a gap; missing_slot_shown_as_gap = 1.000), across levels, or in space. Transects sample the nearest cell.
storms_handling.vertical_scale: Profiles state the stretch on screen, e.g. 'Vertical scale x2'. Without it, profiles read flat (rendering-options.json).
storms_handling.dropped: Extruded walls, storm-motion arrows, arrival times, probability shells, hatch used as severity (supervisor product critic).

risks_ranked: 1. JavaScript scope creep against rule 4 and roadmap Next 9: C1 adds 8 hand-written duties, one of them GLSL; map.js is already 2,155 lines. Mitigation: C2 first; each C1 duty needs owner sign-off.

2. Parallax over-reading: uncorrected tops sit 3-4 km off for a 2 km top and 20-33 km off for a 12-15 km top (parallax.json); a 3D look invites 'holographic' expectations. Mitigation: verbatim legend; no fly-to; correction only with cloud-top heights.

3. Cloud-top validity: no ground truth; Montana valid cells correlate r = -0.62 with Band 13 brightness temperature, and warm brightness temperature at valid high tops is unexplained (goes-aws.json). Mitigation: 'estimated' label; acha metrics; no damage language.
4. Below-ground levels: 0.5 km is 452 m below ground at Billings; 1.0 km sits inside the 50 m margin. A wrong mask mislabels heights. Mitigation: mask with margin; unmasked echo never drawn.
5. -99 and -999 meanings unverified (mrms.json): a wrong guess shows dry areas as gaps or hides gaps. Mitigation: both read 'No radar data'; NSSL table check in P0.

6. Licence and terms: GOES files carry 'Access is restricted to approved users only' while NODD says open (goes-aws.json); Actions terms say develop and test, not CDN use (gh-terms-1, -3). Mitigation: owner or counsel reading before P1; host alternative (ROADMAP Next 8).

7. Schedule reliability: 5-min floor, delays, possible drops, 60-day disable (gh-sched-1, -2, -4, -6). A missed build goes Stale and the echo window gaps. Mitigation: next_expected_utc timestamps; 25-min page-age warning.
8. Phone and cellular cost unmeasured: C1 loops are 14-100 MB per 2 h (rendering-options.json phase_4); no device tests exist.
9. App path: numpy and eccodes (62.16 MB Linux wheels, no Windows eccodes wheel); WebView2 WebGL2 unverified; MSHTML has no WebGL2 (webgl-runtime.json). C2 avoids all three.
10. pydeck's template loads third-party resources and bundles its own MapLibre 5.14.0 and deck.gl ~9.3 (index.j2:6-15; frontend_semver.py). Mitigation: no pydeck HTML page; custom template if C1.
11. Self-test blind spot: HTTP status only (updater.py:141-142); check-app.yml has no browser step. Mitigation: dev-only browser job; smoke_map.py extended.
12. Silent freshness default: unknown feed keys get 3600 s (weather.py:232). Mitigation: loud-failure test on every product key.
13. The sample build uses invented pictures; real frame sizes come only from P0 measurement.
